work_order.root_cause: layout() in src/web/pages.js builds the document shell (head, header, main, footer) and is handed a title it uses for <title> only; it never emits that title as a heading inside <main>. panel() then supplies the first heading on every page at a fixed <h2>, so no document can start at <h1>.
work_order.approach: Emit the page heading once, in the shared layout, as the first child of <main id="main"> and before ${content}, using the same TITLES[route] string the <title> already carries, so the visible heading and the document title can never disagree. Mark it data-testid="page-title" for a stable QA hook. Do NOT demote panel(): its <h2> is already correctly nested beneath a new <h1>, the composer's <h3> is already correctly nested beneath that, and src/web/pages.js:83 is deliberately left alone — the existing test at test/web/pages.test.js:73 matches `panel-error[^]*?<h2>` and the h1 must sit inside <main> (not in the header or outside it) so that document.querySelector('main#main h1,h2,h3,h4,h5,h6') returns H1, which is the exact probe the QA run used to file this. One CSS rule is included because #main is a grid with gap var(--space-3): without it the browser default h1 margin stacks on top of the 24px gap and the page gains ~45px of dead space above the heading.

risks: The h1 is a grid item of #main (display: grid; gap: var(--space-3)). The one CSS rule in files[1] is required, not cosmetic: without it the browser default 0.67em margin stacks on the 24px gap and the default 2em size overpowers the 1.05rem panel headings.

Placing the h1 anywhere but the first child of <main> (in the header, or after ${content}) still renders an h1 and still passes a naive h1 count, but AC-2 fails and the bug is not actually fixed. The probe that found the bug is the first-heading-in-main probe, not the count.

The temptation to 'demote' panel() to <h3> must be resisted: it is not required by the ticket, it would break the existing matcher at test/web/pages.test.js:73 (`panel-error[^]*?<h2>`), and it would leave the composer's <h3> needing a bump to <h4>. h1 -> h2 -> h3 is already well-formed.

src/web/pages.js is the shared layout for every screen, so this is the widest-blast-radius change in the repo even though it is four lines. It touches presentation markup only: no data is read or written differently, no API changes, no new dependency, no host added to env.api_allowlist.

.sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md in files[2] is pipeline-owned documentation. It is not in forbidden_paths, so the diff gate will allow it, but if a reviewer considers it out of band it is safe to drop that one file — it records a hook, it does not affect behaviour.
out_of_scope: Demoting or renumbering panel() headings: h2 under a new h1 is already correct, and the composer's h3 is already correct beneath it.
Changing the drawer's <h2 id="journal-drawer-title"> — it is a dialog label, not a page section, and aria-labelledby depends on the id staying put.
Changing the <title> strings or TITLES. '/' keeping the name 'Command dashboard' while the nav says 'Dashboard' is a separate copy question, not this bug.
Any other accessibility finding (colour contrast, focus order, live-region verbosity): each would ship on its own and belongs in its own ticket.
A landmarks or aria-describedby sweep beyond the heading level: not asked for here and not needed to make this hierarchy well-formed.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add the h1 inside each of the five page functions (dashboard, journal, opportunities, experiments, approvals) rather than in layout().
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Duplicates the same line five times, and any sixth route added later silently reproduces the bug. layout() is the only place all five documents pass through, so the fix belongs there and the change is one edit rather than five.

alternatives_considered.approach: Demote panel() to <h3> and the composer to <h4>, on the reading that the ticket says panel headings are 'demoted beneath' the new heading.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The panels are already <h2>, which is already one level beneath <h1> — nothing needs demoting. It would break test/web/pages.test.js:73, force a second bump for the composer, and change the visual weight of every panel on every screen for no accessibility gain.

alternatives_considered.approach: Make the h1 visually hidden (clip it) so the layout does not change at all.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A sighted user gets no page name, and the ticket's own premise is that the only accessible name today is the <title>, which most screen readers do not surface when navigating by heading. It also dodges rather than answers the visual question the new element raises.

alternatives_considered.approach: Put the h1 in the app header next to the brand, reusing the existing chrome.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It would sit outside <main>, so the main landmark would still have no top-level heading and the exact probe from the bug report would keep returning H2. The h1 belongs inside the landmark it names.

alternatives_considered.approach: Treat the five routes as five tickets, one h1 each.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The cause is one shared line in layout(); five tickets would be five PRs racing to edit the same function. This is a single coherent change, and it is small enough that splitting it costs more than it saves.

assumptions: docs/ui.md names the five screens ('Command dashboard', 'Decision journal', 'Opportunities and experiments', 'Approvals') and prescribes no heading levels, so the ticket's well-formedness rule is the only constraint and nothing in the UI spec conflicts with it.
TITLES[route] is the authoritative screen name in the code today; the h1 reuses it rather than introducing a second map that could drift.
The h1 belongs visually at the top of the page, above the first panel, in every state including loading and error — the screen has a name even when its data has not loaded or has failed.
unknowns: Whether the maintainer wants '/' to read 'Dashboard' (the nav label) or 'Command dashboard' (the TITLES and <title> value) as its visible heading. This plan uses 'Command dashboard' because it makes the heading and the document title identical, which AC-3 then enforces; if the maintainer prefers the nav label, it is a one-word change in TITLES plus the corresponding test, not a redesign.
